dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/5] A total of 372 children in the fourth, fifth, and sixth grades of a semirural elementary school were screened with the Children's Depression Inventory (CDI; Kovacs, 1981) for inclusion in the study. Parental permission for additional assessment was obtained for 39 (64%) of the children who initially scored in excess of 16 on the CDI. These 39 subjects completed a second administration of the CDI. Thirty-one of the children received a total score of 13 or more on the second administration. One subject was later excluded from the study and referred to an external agency when the clinical interview (Childen's Depression Rating Scale-Revised; Poznanski et al., 1984) revealed additional serious nondepressive pathology.
